title: Thorn and Spire Revisited
premise: Felix Crane has spent two decades erasing themselves from every ledger in Greyhollow, a city where magic is contraband and cartographers of the unmapped realms are hunted as heretics. When their date, Wren, appears verbatim in a century-old book of prophecies, Felix learns they were born with a soul already sold to the court beneath the mountain—the price their parents paid for passage out of a burning realm. To survive, Felix must assemble a found family of smugglers, exiled priests, and one very old dragon, steal back their own soul before the last dragon-fire gutters out, and choose between reclaiming the power that comes with it or destroying it forever. In the end, Felix shatters the soul-contract rather than claim it, freeing Wren's prophesied fate and founding a hidden city where the unmapped can finally be drawn.
about_author: Jonah Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who would rather be left alone, from a house full of maps that refuse to stay accurate.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Rule
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. We meet Felix selling charms in Greyhollow's night market, careful, invisible, and quietly lonely, until a charming stranger named Wren asks them to draw a map of somewhere neither of them has been—and the ink moves on its own. Emotional beat: longing cracked open by wonder.

chapters.title: A Century of Small Print
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren discovers their own name and words in a prophecy book dated a hundred years past, and brings it to Felix in panic. Together they realize the prophecy describes tonight exactly—and names Felix as 'the debtor.' Emotional beat: dread of being seen at last.

chapters.title: What the Parents Paid
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Digging through their mother's sealed effects, Felix finds the contract: their soul was sold to the Undercourt beneath the mountain to buy the family's escape. The last dragon-fire that seals the court is guttering, and when it dies, all debts come due. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Recruiting the Damned
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation. Felix and Wren gather allies: Brannoc, a smuggler who owes Felix his life; Sister Ivetta, an exiled priestess who remembers the old rites; and Quill, a pickpocket child who can read dead languages. Emotional beat: the first fragile stitches of found family.

chapters.title: Down the Stair That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. The crew descends through a smuggler's stair into the mountain's roots, navigating a market of things traded away: memories, names, years. Felix sees their own childhood on a shelf, priced and dusty. Emotional beat: grief for what was given up without consent.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Undercourt receives them with velvet menace; its Magistrate offers Felix a bargain—reclaim the soul and inherit the court's power, or leave empty-handed while Wren fulfills the prophecy's darker clause. Emotional beat: temptation wearing the face of justice.

chapters.title: Guttering
chapters.summary: Ivetta's POV. The last dragon-fire flickers toward extinction; the court's power surges as its seal weakens, and Greyhollow above begins to feel the tremors. Ivetta reveals the fire isn't failing—it's being fed on, by the Magistrate himself. Emotional beat: urgency and righteous anger.

chapters.title: The Price of Taking It Back
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix touches their own soul and feels twenty years of borrowed power flood in—enough to unmake the Magistrate, enough to never be small again. Quill nearly dies pulling them back from the edge of keeping it. Emotional beat: the seduction of corruption resisted by love.

chapters.title: Ash and Covenant
chapters.summary: Full ensemble climax. As the dragon-fire gutters out, the crew fights through the collapsing court; Felix chooses not to reclaim but to shatter the contract, feeding their soul back into the flame. The Magistrate unravels with his stolen centuries, and the fire roars back to life. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into freedom.

chapters.title: Mapping What Was Never Lost
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, epilogue tone. Above ground, Greyhollow's outlawed magic stirs openly; Felix, soulless but whole, opens a school of cartography where the unmapped realms are finally drawn—with Wren, Brannoc, Ivetta, and Quill beside them. Emotional beat: quiet joy; family chosen, not inherited.
